clue.text: Around island a coastline mostly polluted is injurious to all

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are wrapped around the island's letter, so Around signals a container
something polluted is spoilt and mixed up, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means nearly all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A dirty shoreline round an island harms everyone who lives there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims COASTLINE to COASTLIN; with A this is shuffled ('polluted') into a string that goes 'Around' I.
explanation.definitionFit: Antisocial behaviour damages the community at large, harming everyone around.

clue.text: Leapt wildly around circle in game

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the ring shape, so around signals a container
wildly suggests the letters of leapt are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone jumped about excitedly in a ring during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' turns LEAPT into PELTA, and 'around' puts that about O.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelota is a Basque ball sport played against a wall, so it is a kind of game.

clue.text: Cricket shot showing bad approach

explanation.surface: A batsman plays a stroke that shows poor technique.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, OFF DRIVE is a driveway that is off, or bad, a poor approach to a house.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an off drive is a stroke hit to the off side; a drive is also the approach road to a house, and off means bad.

clue.text: Moan about receiving a pound in credit

indicators.note: the complaint word takes in the other letters, so receiving signals a container

parts.note: to beef is slang for to moan or complain
L stands for pound, from the Latin libra
a, meaning one, is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles on being handed a pound on trust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is only a link here (to moan about something); BEEF 'receiving' L and I gives BE-LI-EF.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit in the sense of trust or faith: to give credit to a story is to accept it as true.

clue.text: Tease essayist about king's daughter in play

indicators.note: the words for tease go about the king's letter, so about signals a container

parts.note: to cod is British slang for to tease or hoax
R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A writer mocks a monarch's child appearing on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside the tease word. 'Tease' uses an old British slang verb for playing a joke on someone, and the essayist is Charles Lamb under his pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordelia is the youngest of King Lear's three daughters in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Lake that is to the south of East River? Yes and no

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece south of another is written below it, so comes after it

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A lake lying south of New York's East River: is it one or not?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the south of' means IE is written below E and R in this down entry. 'Yes and no' answers the question mark: the lake is E-R with IE under it, but it is not really south of the East River.
explanation.definitionFit: Erie is one of the five Great Lakes of North America.

clue.text: Never again, it's in the past

explanation.surface: A promise it will never happen again, since that is all history.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means just one time and no more, and also formerly, at some earlier time.

clue.text: Woven panel?

parts.note: a panel woven from strands sounds like a basket, but the clue means a building sheet made of compressed plant strands

explanation.surface: A piece of basketwork used as a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: This building board is made of wood or plant strands pressed together, so it is a panel made of interlaced threads.

clue.text: Mother's absurd sporting wear for the holidays?

indicators.note: sporting means wearing or displaying, so the letters are rearranged into the garment

parts.note: taken with its s as part of the letters

explanation.surface: Mum looks ridiculous in her holiday outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' looks like part of the picture (Mum wearing it) but it signals that MOTHERS and ABSURD are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: These knee-length shorts, named after an Atlantic island, are typical warm-weather leisure clothing for travellers.

clue.text: Complaint creates upset

explanation.surface: An illness throws everything into confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be a medical ailment, and an upset is a state of confusion or untidiness.

clue.text: Popular title without a doubt

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a title is a deed proving legal ownership of property

explanation.surface: A well-liked heading, certainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is used to stress a statement as certainly true, like 'truly' or 'certainly'.

clue.text: African country's well ahead

indicators.note: ahead places the word for well in front of the country name

parts.note: so, as in 'so, what next', is a filler word like well
Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: An African nation is doing well and pulling in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African country' looks like the definition, but only 'African' defines; the country is MALI with SO 'ahead' of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Somali is a person from Somalia, a country on the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Developed after decreasing?

explanation.surface: Something grew after it had shrunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'decreasing' as de-creasing, taking the creases out: once something is opened flat, its folds are gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Developed as a story or plan does when it opens out; and something opened flat has had its folds, or creases, taken out.

clue.text: Those who return people to the house

definitions.text: Those who return people to the house

parts.words: Those who return people to the house
parts.note: sounds like people seeing guests home, but means voters returning Members of Parliament to the House of Commons

explanation.surface: Kind folk who walk others back home.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters as a body choose and return members to the House of Commons at an election.

clue.text: Annette is half shattered, living it up

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Annette is only half the woman she was, exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' looks like 'tired', but it signals that ANNETTE, IS and HALF are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the fast lane is to lead an exciting, hectic life of pleasure, like the quickest motorway lane.

clue.text: Due to get in but set up shows rashness

indicators.note: the word for due gets in between the other letters, so this signals a container
in a down entry, set up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: yet means but, as in 'small yet strong'
merit is what someone deserves, what is due to them

explanation.surface: Someone owed money barges in, showing reckless nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns YET into TEY in this down entry, and MERIT goes into it ('to get in').
explanation.definitionFit: Temerity is reckless boldness, a lack of caution.

clue.text: Producer of trifles?

parts.note: trifles sounds like the layered pudding, but here means playthings of little worth

explanation.surface: A dessert cook making sponge, custard and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle is a thing of small value, and a maker of children's playthings makes such things.

clue.text: Opening in wake of ferry port

indicators.note: in wake of means following behind, so the opening comes after the ferry word

parts.note: to ply is to travel a route regularly, as a ferry does
a mouth is an opening, as of a cave or river

explanation.surface: A gap opens behind a ferry as it heads for harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Plymouth is a naval and ferry port on the coast of Devon in south-west England.

clue.text: Prune, one that's turned green?

indicators.note: turned means changed around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A plum that has gone mouldy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' and 'green' suggest fruit gone off; in fact PRUNE and I are rearranged, and 'green' means not yet ripe.
explanation.definitionFit: Green fruit is fruit that has not yet ripened.

clue.text: Shipping guy returning without order

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the reversed word goes round the order
returning means the word for guy is read backwards

parts.note: a guy is a rope, as is a stay on a ship's mast
CH is the Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A sailor comes home in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: STAY 'returning' gives YATS, which goes 'without' (outside) CH. CH is the Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipping is boats taken as a group, and sailing pleasure craft are one kind.

clue.text: Globe flower?

explanation.surface: A round bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe as a whole, a world; and a garden plant of the daisy family with bright blooms.

clue.text: One who'll attend clipper suffering initial cut

indicators.note: the word for clipper loses its first letter, its initial

parts.note: a shearer clips the wool off sheep

explanation.surface: A sheep shearer gets a nick from the very first stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clipper' looks like a ship, but it is SHEARER, who clips fleeces; 'suffering initial cut' drops its S.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend is to listen, and a listener takes in what is said.

clue.text: Another Osiris statue is found inside

indicators.note: the answer sits within the letters of the first two words, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A second image of the Egyptian god turns up indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eros is the winged statue at Piccadilly Circus in London; the letters sit in 'anothER OSiris'.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure on the fountain at Piccadilly Circus is popularly known by the name of the Greek god of love.

clue.text: Cheer up — erasures will be rectified

indicators.note: rectified means put right, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Don't worry: the rubbings-out will be fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassure someone is to comfort them and ease their worries.

clue.text: Canine toiletry?

parts.note: canine suggests a dog's grooming product, but a canine is also a pointed tooth, so this is something for cleaning teeth

explanation.surface: A grooming product for dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: A canine is a pointed human tooth, and this paste is the bathroom product used to clean teeth.

clue.text: Word used in casino at hotel

indicators.note: used in shows the answer is contained within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Language overheard at a hotel's gaming tables.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'casinO AT Hotel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving your word is making a solemn promise, a sworn vow.
